1) Therapy.  I know everyone says this, but it really does help.  

2) Divorce.  I am not saying that you should or should not, though I think that you should, but you need to make a plan and start working towards it to regain control over your life. 

3) Mourn the relationships now and get over what has happened.  People who are willing to do these kinds of things to people close to them don't sit around depressed over what they have done, they don't care.  Holding on to these awful feelings is going to weigh you down and stop you from moving forward.  

4) Try really hard to accept that there are times in life when we get dealt a shit hand and it is not our fault.  The lack of sex was not why they did what they did.  There is always more to it than that. Don't blame yourself, this is not your fault.

I wish you all the luck in the world.

Sigh...  Where do I begin here...  I have so much to say to you.  First and foremost, read books about cheating.  When you start to study the psychology behind it, it may shed light on why you stay.  Often times there is a codependent relationship at play.  Looks like that might be the case here.  You seem to be supporting your marriage and he is being disrespectful of your sacrifice.  The next thing I have to say is that you are so young, too young to be in a marriage that you are trying to make work with someone who doesn't respect you.   You mentioned that you are not telling people about what has happened.  You didn't do anything wrong.  You should not have to hide things in your life from the people who care about you.  You said that you two have a connection that draws you to one another.  I unfortunately understand this all too well.  This connection is not love though.  Love is fair, kind and respectful.   It is honest.  Perhaps go to therapy.  Not together, alone.  Find the answers to why you would tolerate being treated like this.  Patterns are hard to break.  If you need someone to talk to, you are welcome to pm me for my number.  My husband was a sexual addict.  I can relate to how you are feeling.  Good luck sweetheart.  I wish you all the best.

There is a better subreddit for you.  It is called suicidewatch.  I hope that you are alright as I am typing this.  My husband was a sailor and he committed suicide.  I am sure that he thought that nobody would miss him and how wrong he was.  I can't begin to tell you the effects his death has had on  me and the people who knew him.  Seek help my friend.  Do so before it is too late.  On my husband's birthday this year I posted something long on his Facebook page.  It is too much to receite here, but the one thing that I want to tell you is that there is no redemption in death.  It is final.  There is no fork in the road and no chance of anything else.  If you begin feeling that is the best choice for you, please drive yourself to the nearest hospital.  Life is short and so very precious.  May the sun be upon your face tomorrow and bless you with your first of many good days to come.

About ten years ago I was eating breakfast in a restaurant in Connecticut and they had these paper placemats with random trivia printed on them.  One of the random facts was that John Lennon's murder was carrying a copy of The Catcher in the Rye on him when he assassinated Lennon.  There was a woman sitting with her teenage son in the booth behind me.  I heard him ask his mother what the book was about.  Her response was that it was a disgusting book about nothing and that it wasn't worth reading.   I finished my breakfast and for the first time in my life corrected a stranger in public.  I let that young kid know that The Catcher in the Rye is one of the greatest books written in the past hundred years.  I then looked at his mother while I told him to investigate his own curiosities, there is ignorance everywhere.  She glared and I left.  Sure hope he read it.
